summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and left shoulder pain following a fall. She had recently completed treatment for C. diff and presented with a recurrence, confirmed by a positive stool toxin test. She was started on high-dose oral vancomycin, with gradual improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms. During admission, she was found to have acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, evidenced by pulmonary edema on chest imaging, which improved with IV and oral diuretics. She developed transient worsening of renal function, likely due to fluid overload, which stabilized with diuresis. A transfusion of one unit of packed red blood cells was given for symptomatic anemia, with good response. Chest pain was evaluated and attributed to a combination of heart failure, GERD, and abdominal inflammation, rather than acute coronary syndrome. She remained DNR/DNI throughout. At discharge, she was stable, transitioning to extended care with a plan to continue vancomycin under Infectious Disease guidance and monitor fluid status closely.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Diabetes with other specified manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Late effects of cerebrovascular disease, hemiplegia affecting unspecified side
